O.outcome_detail: accuracy of predicting grade 8 Algebra I CST proficiency

result.effect: accuracy increased from 69% to 75% (+6 percentage points)

cells.quote: Using students’ grade 6 math CST scale score rather than proficiency status increases the accuracy of algebra I placement decisions in grade 8 from 69 percent to 75 percent.
cells.note: The study compares prediction approaches using observational assessment data; it does not randomly assign placement.

O.outcome_detail: odds of achieving proficiency on the grade 8 Algebra I CST

result.effect: a one-percentage-point increase was associated with a 26% increase in the odds

cells.quote: For example, holding other predictor scores constant, a one percent-age point increase on MDTP topic area 6, integers, is associated with a 26 percent increase in the odds of achieving proficiency on the algebra I CST in grade 8.
cells.note: The association was estimated while controlling for grade 6 CST scale score; it is not a causal treatment effect.

O.outcome_detail: accuracy of predicting grade 8 Algebra I CST proficiency

cells.quote: Models using the grade 6 CST scale scores alone, the grade 7 CST scale scores alone, the grade 7 MDTP, or CST scale scores in combination with the MDTP scores all resulted in accurate predictions of success between 75 and 78 percent of the time.
cells.note: The text reports similar prediction accuracies across assessments but does not report a significance test or establish a definitive directional difference.
